If <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\mathfrak g)$</tex> is the universal enveloping algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak g$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\mathfrak g)^K$</tex> will denote the centralizer of K in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\mathfrak g)$</tex>. Also let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P:U(\mathfrak g)\longrightarrow U(\mathfrak k)\otimes U(\mathfrak a)$</tex> be the projection map corresponding to the direct sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\mathfrak g)=(U(\mathfrak k)\otimes U(\mathfrak a))\oplus U(\mathfrak g)\mathfrak n$</tex> associated to an Iwasawa decomposition of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> adapted to K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>. In this paper, we give a characterization of the image of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U(\mathfrak g)^K$</tex> under the injective antihomorphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P:U(\mathfrak g)^K\longrightarrow U(\mathfrak k)^M\otimes U(\mathfrak a)$</tex>, considered by Lepowsky in [12], when G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> is isomorphic to the rank 1 real form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm F}^{-20}_4$</tex> of the exceptional Lie group F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>.

articleTitle: On the Polynomial Convexity of the Union of Three Totally Real Planes in ℂ2
abstract: In this paper, we discuss local polynomial convexity at the origin of the union of three totally real planes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb C^2$</tex>. The planes, say P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>,P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> satisfy a mild transversality condition: P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>∩P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>={0}, j=1,2, which enables us to view them in Weinstock's normal form, that is, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_0=\mathbb R^2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_j=M(A_j):=(A_j+i\mathbb I)\mathbb R^2$</tex>, j=1,2, where each A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> is a 2×2 matrix with real entries. Weinstock solved the problem completely for two totally real planes (in fact, for pairs of transverse, maximally totally real subspaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb C^n,n\geq2$</tex>). Using Weinstock's ideas for simplifying the model for P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>∪P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>∪P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, we provide an open condition for the local polynomial convexity at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\in \mathbb C^2$</tex> of the union of three totally real planes.

articleTitle: Smooth Orbital Varieties and Orbital Varieties with a Dense B-Orbit
abstract: The orbital varieties are the irreducible components of the intersection between a nilpotent orbit and a Borel subalgebra of a reductive Lie algebra. Orbital varieties arise in representation theory as the geometric analogs of the enveloping algebra’s primitive ideals. They are also related to the irreducible components of the Springer fibers. In type A, the orbital varieties have a convenient parameterization by standard Young tableaux, in particular, one has a natural duality on the set of orbital varieties induced by the Young tableau transposition. In this paper, we provide several combinatorial criteria to guarantee that an orbital variety is smooth or contains a dense orbit for the action of the Borel subgroup B. We point out that, in all the cases that we can compute, the smooth orbital varieties and the orbital varieties which have a dense B-orbit correspond via the aforementioned duality.

articleTitle: The Nontrivial Zeros of Period Polynomials of Modular Forms Lie on the Unit Circle
abstract: We show that all but five of the zeros of the period polynomial associated to a Hecke cusp form are on the unit circle.

articleTitle: Improved Bounds on Sárközy’s Theorem for Quadratic Polynomials
abstract: We extend the best-known bound on the largest subset of {1,2,…,N} with no square differences to the largest possible class of quadratic polynomials.

articleTitle: Global Second Derivative Estimates for the Second Boundary Value Problem of the Prescribed Affine Mean Curvature and Abreu's Equations
abstract: In this paper, we prove the global second derivative estimates for the second boundary value problem of the prescribed affine mean curvature equation, where the affine mean curvature is only assumed to be in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>. Our result extends previous result by Trudinger and Wang in the case of globally bounded affine mean curvature and also covers Abreu's equation.

articleTitle: Dynamics of the Symmetric Eigenvalue Problem with Shift Strategies
abstract: A common algorithm for the computation of eigenvalues of real symmetric tridiagonal matrices is the iteration of certain special maps F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σ</inf> called shifted QR steps. Such maps preserve spectrum and a natural common domain is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal T_{\Lambda}$</tex>, the manifold of real symmetric tridiagonal matrices conjugate to the diagonal matrix Λ. More precisely, a (generic) shift <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s \in \mathbb R$</tex> defines a map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_s:\mathcal T_{\Lambda}\rightarrow\mathcal T_{\Lambda}$</tex>. A strategy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma:\mathcal T_{\Lambda}\rightarrow \mathbb R$</tex> specifies the shift to be applied at T so that F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σ</inf>(T)=F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σ(T)</inf>(T). Good shift strategies should lead to fast deflation: some off-diagonal coordinate tends to zero, allowing for reduction of the problem to submatrices. For topological reasons, continuous shift strategies do not obtain fast deflation; many standard strategies are indeed discontinuous. Practical implementation only gives rise systematically to bottom deflation, convergence to zero of the lowest off-diagonal entry b(T). For most shift strategies, convergence to zero of b(T) is cubic, |b(F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σ</inf>(T))|=Θ(|b(T)|<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>) for k=3. The existence of arithmetic progressions in the spectrum of T sometimes implies instead quadratic convergence, k=2. The complete integrability of the Toda lattice and the dynamics at non-smooth points are central to our discussion. The text does not assume knowledge of numerical linear algebra.

Let (M,F) be a connected Finsler space and d the distance function of (M,F). A Clifford translation is an isometry ρ of (M,F) of constant displacement, in other words such that d(x,ρ(x)) is a constant function on M. In this paper, we consider a connected simply connected symmetric Finsler space and a discrete subgroup Γ of the full group of isometries. We prove that the quotient manifold (M,F)/Γ is a homogeneous Finsler space if and only if Γ consists of Clifford translations of (M,F). In the process of the proof of the main theorem, we classify all the Clifford translations of symmetric Finsler spaces.

articleTitle: Generic Bases for Cluster Algebras From the Cluster Category
abstract: Inspired by recent work of Geiss–Leclerc–Schröer, we use Hom-finite cluster categories to give a good candidate set for a basis of (upper) cluster algebras with coefficients arising from quivers. This set consists of generic values taken by the cluster character on objects having the same index. If the matrix associated to the quiver is of full rank, then we prove that the elements in this set are linearly independent. If the cluster algebra arises from the setting of Geiss–Leclerc–Schröer, then we obtain the basis found by these authors. We show how our point of view agrees with the spirit of conjectures of Fock–Goncharov concerning the parametrization of a basis of the upper cluster algebra by points in the tropical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal X$</tex>-variety.

articleTitle: Generalized Rabinowitz Floer Homology and Coisotropic Intersections
abstract: In this paper, we extend Rabinowitz Floer homology theory which has been established and extensively studied for hypersurfaces to coisotropic submanifolds of higher codimension. With this generalized version of Rabinowitz Floer homology theory, we explore the coisotropic intersection problem which interpolates between the Lagrangian intersection problem and the closed orbit problem. To be specific, we study the existence of leafwise intersection points on contact coisotropic submanifolds and the displaceability of stable coisotropic submanifolds.

articleTitle: Geometry of Contactomorphism Groups, Contact Rigidity, and Contact Dynamics in Jet Spaces
abstract: For a closed connected manifold N, we establish the existence of geometric structures on various subgroups of the contactomorphism group of the standard contact jet space J<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>N, as well as on the group of contactomorphisms of the standard contact T*N×S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> generated by compactly supported contact vector fields. The geometric structures are biinvariant partial orders (for J<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>N and T*N×S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) and biinvariant integer-valued metrics (T*N×S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> only). We prove some forms of contact rigidity in T*N×S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, namely that certain (possibly singular) subsets of the form X×S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> cannot be disjoined from the zero section by a contact isotopy, and in addition that there are restrictions on commuting products of contactomorphisms. Finally, we prove multiplicity results for orbits of certain contact flows in T*N×S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> with Legendrian boundary conditions, which in particular apply to Reeb chords. The method is that of generating functions for Legendrians in jet spaces.

articleTitle: Zeros of a Family of Approximations of the Riemann Zeta-Function
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F_N(s)=\Sigma_{n\leq N}n^{-s}$</tex> be a partial sum of the Riemann zeta-function, ζ(s), and set ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(s)=F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(s)+χ(s)F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(1−s), where s=σ+it is a complex variable. The approximate functional equation for ζ(s) tells us that ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(s) is a good approximation of ζ(s) when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=\sqrt{t/2\pi}$</tex>. Here, we investigate the distribution of zeros of ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(s) when N is independent of t. We determine “critical” strips in which most of the zeros lie (on and off the Riemann Hypothesis), the number of zeros of ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(s) in rectangles, and lower bounds for the number of zeros of ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>(s) on the critical line <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma =\frac {1}{2}$</tex>. In particular, we show that when N≤T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o(1)</sup>, 100% of the zeros with ordinates in [0,T] lie on the critical line and are simple.

articleTitle: Theta Lifting and Cohomology Growth in p-adic Towers
abstract: We use the theta lift to study the multiplicity with which certain automorphic representations of cohomological type occur in a family of congruence covers of an arithmetic manifold. When the family of covers is a so-called p-adic congruence tower, we obtain sharp asymptotics for the number of representations that occur as lifts. When combined with theorems on the surjectivity of the theta lift due to Howe and Li, and Bergeron, Millson, and Moeglin, this allows us to verify certain cases of a conjecture of Sarnak and Xue.

articleTitle: Waring Problem for Finite Quasisimple Groups
abstract: The classical Waring problem deals with expressing every natural number as a sum of g(k) kth powers. Similar problems for finite simple groups were studied recently, and in this paper we study them for finite quasisimple groups G. We show that for a fixed group word w≠1 and for G of sufficiently large order we have w(G)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>=G, namely every element of G is a product of three values of w. For various families of finite quasisimple groups, including covers of alternating groups, we obtain a stronger result, namely w(G)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=G. However, in contrast with the case of simple groups studied in [14], we show that w(G)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=G need not hold for all large G; moreover, if k>2, then x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> is not surjective on infinitely many finite quasisimple groups. The case k=2 turns out to be exceptional. Indeed, our last result shows that every element of a finite quasisimple group is a product of two squares. This can be regarded as a noncommutative analog of Lagrange’s four squares theorem.

articleTitle: On the Conditions to Extend Ricci Flow(III)
abstract: We simplify and improve the curvature estimates in [8] and [9]. Furthermore, we develop some new estimates of volume ratio for the Ricci flow with bounded scalar curvature. These estimates can be applied to study the singularities of the Ricci flow and convergence properties of the Kähler Ricci flow.

articleTitle: Global Smoothing for the Periodic KdV Evolution
abstract: The Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation with periodic boundary conditions is considered. It is shown that for H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup> initial data, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s \gt-\frac {1}{2}$</tex>, and for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s_1\lt\ \min(3s+1,s+1)$</tex>, the difference of the nonlinear and linear evolutions is in Hs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> for all times, with at most polynomially growing Hs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> norm. The result also extends to KdV with a smooth, mean zero, time-dependent potential in the case s≥0. Our result and a theorem of Oskolkov for the Airy evolution imply that if one starts with continuous and bounded variation initial data, then the solution of KdV (given by the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> theory of Bourgain) is a continuous function of space and time. In addition, we demonstrate smoothing for the defocusing modified KdV equation on the torus for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s \gt\frac {1}{2}$</tex>.
Upper bounds on projective rigidity of each homogeneously embedded homogeneous variety are determined; and a new, invariant characterization of the Fubini forms is given.

articleTitle: Unirationality of Hurwitz Spaces of Coverings of Degree ≤5
abstract: Let Y be a smooth, projective curve of genus g≥1 over the complex numbers. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H^0_{d,A}(Y)$</tex> be the Hurwitz space that parameterizes equivalence classes of coverings π:X→Y of degree d simply branched in n=2e points, such that the monodromy group is S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\det(\pi_*\mathcal O_X/\mathcal O_Y)^{\vee}$</tex> is isomorphic to a fixed line bundle A of degree e. We prove that, when d=3,4, or 5 and n is sufficiently large (precise bounds are given), the Hurwitz space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H^0_{d,A}(Y)$</tex> is unirational. If, in addition, (e,2)=1 (when d=3), (e,6)=1 (when d=4), and (e,10)=1 (when d=5), then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal H^0_{d,A}(Y)$</tex> is rational.

articleTitle: Brändén's Conjectures on the Boros–Moll Polynomials
abstract: We prove two conjectures of Brändén on the real-rootedness of the polynomials Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x) and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x) which are related to the Boros–Moll polynomials P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x). In fact, we show that both Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x) and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x) form Sturm sequences. The first conjecture implies the 2-log-concavity of P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x), and the second conjecture implies the 3-log-concavity of P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x).

articleTitle: The Euler–Poisson System in 2D: Global Stability of the Constant Equilibrium Solution
abstract: We consider the (repulsive) Euler–Poisson system for the electrons in two dimensions and prove that small smooth perturbations of a constant background exist for all time and remain smooth (never develop shocks). This extends to 2D the work of Guo 6.

articleTitle: Infinite-Dimensional Nonpositively Curved Symmetric Spaces of Finite Rank
abstract: This paper concerns a study of three families of noncompact type symmetric spaces of infinite dimension. Although they have infinite dimension they have finite rank. More precisely, we show that they have finite telescopic dimension. We also show the existence of Furstenberg maps for some group actions on these spaces. Such maps appear as a first step toward superrigidity results.

articleTitle: A Decay Estimate for a Wave Equation with Trapping and a Complex Potential
abstract: In this brief note, we consider a wave equation that has both trapping and a complex potential. For this problem, we prove a uniform bound on the energy and a Morawetz (or integrated local energy decay) estimate. The equation is a model problem for certain scalar equations appearing in the Maxwell and linearized Einstein systems on the exterior of a rotating black hole.

articleTitle: On the Asymptotics of the Ray–Singer Analytic Torsion for Compact Hyperbolic Manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of the analytic torsion for compact oriented hyperbolic manifolds with respect to certain rays of representations obtained by restriction of irreducible representations of the group of isometries of the hyperbolic space.

articleTitle: Large Deviations of Empirical Measures of Zeros on Riemann Surfaces
abstract: We determine a large deviations principle (LDP) for the empirical measure of zeros of random holomorphic sections s of random line bundles L→X over a Riemann surface X of genus g≥1. Zeitouni and Zelditch [27] proved such an LDP in the g=0 case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ \mathbb C\mathbb P^1$</tex> using an explicit formula for the joint probability current (JPC) of zeros of Gaussian random polynomials. The main purpose of this article is to define Gaussian-type measures on the “vortex moduli space” of all holomorphic sections of all line bundles of degree N and to calculate its JPC as a volume form on the configuration space X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(N)</sup> of N points of X.

articleTitle: Parabolic Systems with Measurable Coefficients in Reifenberg Domains
abstract: We consider a parabolic system in divergence form with measurable coefficients in a nonsmooth bounded domain to obtain a global gradient estimate for the weak solution in the setting of Orlicz space which is a natural generalization of L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> space. The coefficients are assumed to be merely measurable in one spatial variable and have small bounded mean oscillation semi-norms in all the other variables. The boundary of the domain can be locally approximated by a hyperplane, a so-called δ-Reifenberg domain which is beyond the Lipschitz category.

Results of several authors have, in the last 20 years or so, associated Galois representations of degree n with cuspidal automorphic representations of adelic GL(n), over totally real or CM fields, satisfying certain conditions. We prove that, even in the case when the natural n-dimensional Galois representations cannot be constructed, the automorphic representations satisfy the Ramanujan conjecture at unramified primes.

articleTitle: Local Estimates for Elliptic Equations Arising in Conformal Geometry
abstract: In this paper, we consider a Yamabe-type problem for higher-order curvatures on manifolds with totally geodesic boundaries. We prove local gradient and second-derivative estimates for solutions to the fully nonlinear elliptic equations associated with the problems.

articleTitle: Néron Models of Formally Finite Type
abstract: We introduce Néron models of formally finite (ff) type for uniformly rigid spaces, thereby generalizing formal Néron models for rigid-analytic groups as they had been studied by Bosch and Schlöter. As an application, we show that Néron models of ff type provide a link between the Néron model of an algebraic torus and the Néron model of an abelian variety with potentially ordinary reduction.

articleTitle: The Zeta Functions of Complexes from Sp(4)
abstract: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with a finite residue field. To a two-dimensional finite complex X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf> arising as the quotient of the Bruhat–Tits building X associated to Sp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(F) by a discrete torsion-free co-compact subgroup Γ of PGSp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(F), associate the zeta function Z(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf>,u) which counts geodesic tailless cycles contained in the 1-skeleton of X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf>. Using a representation-theoretic approach, we obtain two closed-form expressions for Z(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf>,u) as a rational function in u. Equivalent statements for X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf> being a Ramanujan complex are given in terms of vertex, edge, and chamber adjacency operators, respectively. The zeta functions of such Ramanujan complexes are distinguished by satisfying the Riemann hypothesis.

articleTitle: New Examples of Stable Bundles on Calabi–Yau Three-Folds
abstract: In this paper, we present a construction of stable bundles on Calabi–Yau three-folds using the method of bundle extensions. This construction applies to any given Calabi–Yau three-fold with h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,1</sup>>1. We give examples of stable bundles of ranks 2 and 4 constructed out of pure geometric data of the given Calabi–Yau space. As an application, we find that some of these bundles satisfy the physical constraint imposed by heterotic string anomaly cancellation.

articleTitle: Generalized and Quasi-Localizations of Braid Group Representations
abstract: We develop a theory of localization for braid group representations associated with objects in braided fusion categories and, more generally, to Yang–Baxter (YB) operators in monoidal categories. The essential problem is to determine when a family of braid representations can be uniformly modelled upon a tensor power of a fixed vector space in such a way that the braid group generators act “locally”. Although related to the notion of (quasi-)fiber functors for fusion categories, remarkably, such localizations can exist for representations associated with objects of non-integral dimension. We conjecture that such localizations exist precisely when the object in question has dimension the square-root of an integer and prove several key special cases of the conjecture.

articleTitle: Astuce de Salberger et Zéro-cycles Sur Certaines Fibrations
abstract: Résumé. On démontre que l’obstruction de Brauer–Manin est la seule au principe de Hasse et à l’approximation faible pour les zéro-cycles sur certaines fibrations au-dessus d’une courbe lisse ou au-dessus de l’espace projectif. L’exactitude d’une suite de type global-local pour les groupes de Chow des zéro-cycles est aussi établie pour ces variétés. La nouveauté principale est que les hypothéses arithmétiques sont supposées seulement sur les fibres au-dessus d’un sous-ensemble hilbertien généralisé, de plus, on permet l’existence des fibres géométriquement non intègres. We prove that the Brauer–Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to the Hasse principle and to weak approximation for zero-cycles on certain fibrations over a smooth curve or over the projective space. The exactness of a sequence of global-local type for Chow groups of zero-cycles is also established for these varieties. The principal novelty is that the arithmetic hypotheses are supposed only on the fibers over a generalized Hilbertian subset, moreover, we permit the existence of geometrically non integral fibers.

articleTitle: Symmetric Chain Decomposition for Cyclic Quotients of Boolean Algebras and Relation to Cyclic Crystals
abstract: The quotient of a Boolean algebra by a cyclic group is proved to have a symmetric chain decomposition. This generalizes earlier work of Griggs, Killian and Savage on the case of prime order, giving an explicit construction for any order, prime or composite. The combinatorial map specifying how to proceed downward in a symmetric chain is shown to be a natural cyclic analog of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {sl}_2$</tex> lowering operator in the theory of crystal bases.

articleTitle: Jucys–Murphy Elements and Unitary Matrix Integrals
abstract: In this paper, we study the relationship between polynomial integrals on the unitary group and the conjugacy class expansion of symmetric functions in Jucys–Murphy elements. Our main result is an explicit formula for the top coefficients in the class expansion of monomial symmetric functions in Jucys–Murphy elements, from which we recover the first-order asymptotics of polynomial integrals over U(N) as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\rightarrow\infty$</tex>. Our results on class expansion include an analog of Macdonald’s result for the top connection coefficients of the class algebra, a generalization of Stanley and Olshanski’s result on the polynomiality of content statistics on Plancherel-random partitions, and an exact formula for the multiplicity of the class of full cycles in the expansion of a complete symmetric function in Jucys–Murphy elements. The latter leads to a new combinatorial interpretation of the Carlitz–Riordan central factorial numbers.

The purpose of this paper is to generalize the (Poisson) Optimal Reduction Theorem in Ortega and Ratiu [Momentum Maps and Hamiltonian Reduction. Progress in Mathematics 222. Boston, MA: Birkhäuser. xxxiv, 497pp., 2004] to general proper Lie group actions on Dirac manifolds, formulated both in terms of point and orbit reduction. A comparison to general standard singular Dirac reduction is given emphasizing the desingularization role played by optimal reduction.

articleTitle: Abundance of Real Lines on Real Projective Hypersurfaces
abstract: We show that a generic real projective n-dimensional hypersurface of degree 2n−1 contains many real lines, namely not less than (2n−1)!!, which is approximately the square root of the number of complex lines. This estimate is based on the interpretation of a suitable signed count of the lines as the Euler number of an appropriate bundle.

articleTitle: K-Theoretic J-Functions of Type A Flag Varieties
abstract: The J-function in Gromov–Witten theory is a generating function for one-point genus zero Gromov–Witten invariants with descendants. Here, we give formulas for the quantum K-theoretic J-functions of type A flag manifolds. As an application, we prove the quantum K-theoretic J-function version of the abelian–nonabelian correspondence for Grassmannians and products of projective space.

articleTitle: The Descriptive Set Theory of C*-algebra Invariants
abstract: We establish the Borel computability of various C*-algebra invariants, including the Elliott invariant and the Cuntz semigroup. As applications, we deduce that AF algebras are classifiable by countable structures, and that a conjecture of Winter and the second author for nuclear separable simple C*-algebras cannot be disproved by appealing to known standard Borel structures on these algebras.

articleTitle: The Maximal Density of Product-Free Sets in ℤ/nℤ
abstract: This paper studies the maximal size of product-free sets in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$</tex>. These are sets of residues for which there is no solution to ab≡c (mod n), with a,b,c being in the set. In a previous paper, we constructed an infinite sequence of integers (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i≥1</inf> and product-free sets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal S_i$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Z/n_i\mathbb Z$</tex> such that the density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\mathcal S_i|/n_i\rightarrow1$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i\rightarrow \infty$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\mathcal S_i|$</tex> denotes the cardinality of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal S_i$</tex>. Here, we obtain matching, up to constants, upper and lower bounds on the maximal attainable density as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\rightarrow\infty$</tex>.

articleTitle: An Index Theorem on Anti-Self-Dual Orbifolds
abstract: An index theorem for the anti-self-dual deformation complex on anti-self-dual orbifolds with singularities conjugate to ADE-type is proved. In 1988, Claude Lebrun gave examples of scalar-flat Kähler ALE metrics with negative mass, on the total space of the bundle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal O(-n)$</tex> over S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A corollary of this index theorem is that the moduli space of anti-self-dual ALE metrics near each of these metrics has dimension at least 4n−12, and thus for n≥4 the LeBrun metrics admit a plethora of nontrivial anti-self-dual deformations.

First, we apply Thurston’s construction of pseudo-Anosov homeomorphisms to grid graphs and obtain translation surfaces whose Veech groups are commensurable to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(m,n,\infty)$</tex> triangle groups. These surfaces were first discovered by Bouw and Möller, however, our treatment of the surfaces differs. We construct these surfaces by gluing together polygons in two ways. We use these elementary descriptions to compute the Veech groups, resolve primitivity questions, and describe the surfaces algebraically. Second, we show that some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(m,n,\infty)$</tex> triangle groups cannot arise as Veech groups. This generalizes the work of Hubert and Schmidt.

articleTitle: Polytopes with Mass Linear Functions II: The Four-Dimensional Case
abstract: This paper continues the analysis begun in Polytopes with mass linear functions, Part I of the structure of smooth moment polytopes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\triangle\subset\mathfrak t^*$</tex> that support a mass linear function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\in \mathfrak t$</tex>. As explained there, besides its purely combinatorial interest, this question is relevant to the study of the homomorphism π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>)→π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(Symp(M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf>,ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf>)) from the fundamental group of the torus T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> to that of the group of symplectomorphisms of the 2n-dimensional symplectic toric manifold (M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf>,ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Δ</inf>) associated to Δ. In Part I, we made a general investigation of this question and classified all mass linear pairs (Δ,H) in dimensions up to 3. The main result of the current paper is a classification of all four-dimensional examples. Along the way, we investigate the properties of general constructions such as fibrations, blow ups, and expansions (or wedges), describing their effect on both moment polytopes and mass linear functions. We end by discussing the relation of mass linearity to Shelukhin’s notion of full mass linearity. The two concepts agree in dimensions up to and including 4. However, full mass linearity may be the more natural concept when considering the question of which blowups preserve mass linearity.

articleTitle: Stochastic Homogenization of Level-Set Convex Hamilton–Jacobi Equations
abstract: We present a simple, new proof for the stochastic homogenization of quasiconvex (level-set convex) Hamilton–Jacobi equations set in stationary ergodic environments. Our approach, which is new even in the convex case, yields more information about the qualitative behavior of the effective nonlinearity.

articleTitle: A Note on the Boundedness of Riesz Transform for Some Subelliptic Operators
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb M$</tex> be a smooth connected noncompact manifold endowed with a smooth measure μ and a smooth locally subelliptic diffusion operator L satisfying L1=0, and that is symmetric with respect to μ. We show that if L satisfies, with a nonnegative curvature parameter ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, the generalized curvature inequality in (2.9), then the Riesz transform is bounded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^p(\mathbb M)$</tex> for every p>1, that is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\parallel\sqrt{\Gamma ((-L)^{-1/2}f)}\parallel_p \leq C_p\parallel f\parallel_p,\quad f\in C^{\infty}_0(\mathbb M),$$</tex> where Γ is the carré du champ associated to L. Our results apply in particular to all Sasakian manifolds whose horizontal Tanaka–Webster Ricci curvature is nonnegative, all Carnot groups with step two, and wide subclasses of principal bundles over Riemannian manifolds whose Ricci curvature is nonnegative.

articleTitle: Odds and Ends on Finite Group Actions and Traces
abstract: In this article, we study several problems related to virtual traces for finite group actions on schemes of finite type over an algebraically closed field. We also discuss applications to fixed-point sets. Our results generalize previous results obtained by Deligne, Laumon, Serre, and others.

articleTitle: Heegaard Floer Correction Terms and Dedekind–Rademacher Sums
abstract: We derive a closed formula for the Heegaard Floer correction terms of lens spaces in terms of the classical Dedekind sum and its generalization, the Dedekind–Rademacher sum. Our proof relies on a reciprocity formula for the correction terms established by Ozsváth and Szabó. A consequence of our result is that the Casson–Walker invariant of a lens space equals the average of its Heegaard Floer correction terms. Additionally, we find an obstruction for the equality and equality with opposite sign, of two correction terms of the same lens space. Using this obstruction we are able to derive an optimal upper bound on the number of vanishing correction terms of lens spaces with square order second cohomology.

articleTitle: A Note on Maximal Lattice Growth in SO(1,n)
abstract: We show that the number of maximal lattices with volume less than v is at least exponential in v. To do this, we construct families of noncommensurable Gromov/Piatetski-Shapiro manifolds having the same volume.

articleTitle: A Simple Sharp Weighted Estimate of the Dyadic Shifts on Metric Spaces with Geometric Doubling
abstract: We give a short and simple polynomial estimate of the norm of weighted dyadic shift, which is linear in the norm of the weight. The method uses Bellman function technique in an essential way.

articleTitle: Lipschitz Correspondence between Metric Measure Spaces and Random Distance Matrices
abstract: Given a metric space with a Borel probability measure, for each integer N, we obtain a probability distribution on N × N distance matrices by considering the distances between pairs of points in a sample consisting of N points chosen independently from the metric space with respect to the given measure. We show that this gives an asymptotically bi-Lipschitz relation between metric measure spaces and the corresponding distance matrices. This is an effective version of a result of Vershik that metric measure spaces are determined by associated distributions on infinite random matrices.

articleTitle: Ricci Flat Kähler Metrics with Edge Singularities
abstract: We construct Ricci flat Kähler metrics with cone singularities along a complex hypersurface. This construction is inspired in part by R. Mazzeo's program in the case of a negative Einstein constant, and uses the linear theory developed recently by S. Donaldson.

articleTitle: Locally Divergent Orbits on Hilbert Modular Spaces
abstract: We describe the closures of locally divergent orbits under the action of tori on Hilbert modular spaces of rank r≥2. In particular, we prove that if D is a maximal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}$</tex>-split torus acting on a real Hilbert modular space, then every locally divergent nonclosed orbit is dense for r>2 and its closure is a finite union of tori orbits for r=2. Our results confirm an orbit rigidity conjecture of G. A. Margulis in all cases except for (i) r=2 and (ii) r>2 and the Hilbert modular space corresponds to a CM-field; in the cases (i) and (ii), our results contradict the conjecture. As an application, we describe the set of values at integral points of collections of nonproportional, split, binary, quadratic forms over number fields.

articleTitle: Beilinson–Bernstein Localization Over ℚ and Periods of Automorphic Forms
abstract: This article explains an approach to Beilinson–Bernstein localization over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Q$</tex>, when G is the group attached to a Shimura variety S(G,X). We develop a theory of compatible rational structures, over appropriately chosen number fields, on discrete series Harish-Chandra modules over the groups attached to the conjugate Shimura varieties. In this way, we can endow automorphic representations of discrete series type at infinity with canonical rational structures over natural coefficient fields, and show that these are compatible with Galois conjugation.

We prove that a normal variety contains finitely many maximal quasi-projective open subvarieties. As a corollary, we obtain the following generalization of the Chevalley–Kleiman projectivity criterion: a normal variety is quasi-projective if and only if every finite subset is contained in an affine open subvariety. The proof builds on a strategy of Włodarczyk, using results of Boissière, Gabber, and Serman.

articleTitle: Topological Expansion in the Cubic Random Matrix Model
abstract: In this paper, we study the topological expansion in the cubic random matrix model, and we evaluate explicitly the expansion coefficients for genus 0 and 1. For genus 0 our formula coincides with the one in [6]. For higher genus, we obtain the asymptotic behavior of the coefficients in the expansion as the number of vertices of the associated graphs tends to infinity. Our study is based on the Riemann–Hilbert problem, string equations, and the Toda equation.

articleTitle: Characterization of γ-Factors: the Asai Case
abstract: Let E be a separable quadratic extension of a locally compact field F of positive characteristic. Asai γ-factors are defined for smooth irreducible representations π of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(E). If σ is the Weil–Deligne representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal W_E$</tex> corresponding to π under the local Langlands correspondence, we show that the Asai γ-factor is the same as the Deligne–Langlands γ-factor of the Weil–Deligne representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal W_F$</tex> obtained from σ under tensor induction. This is achieved by proving that Asai γ-factors are characterized by their local properties together with their role in global functional equations for L-functions. As an immediate application, we establish the stability property of γ-factors under twists by highly ramified characters.

articleTitle: Blow up of Solutions and Traveling Waves to the Two-Component μ-Camassa–Holm System
abstract: The integrable two-component μ-Camassa–Holm system is a mid-way system between the two-component Camassa–Holm and the two-component Hunter–Saxton systems. The initial-value problem and traveling-wave solutions to the two-component μ-Camassa–Holm system in the periodic setting are investigated in this paper. Blow-up scenarios for strong solutions are established. Several blow-up data and blow-up rate for strong solutions are provided. Finally, the existence of smooth periodic traveling-wave solutions is determined.

articleTitle: A Remark on the Alexander Polynomial Criterion for the Bi-orderability of Fibered 3-manifold Groups
abstract: By studying the maximal ordered abelian quotient of bi-ordered groups, we show that Clay–Rolfsen’s obstruction of bi-orderability, which uses the classical Alexander polynomial, is not strengthened using the twisted Alexander polynomials for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb Q$</tex>-linear representation having a finite image. This contrasts with many known applications of the Alexander polynomial.

articleTitle: The A∞ de Rham Theorem and Integration of Representations up to Homotopy
abstract: We use Chen’s iterated integrals to integrate representations up to homotopy. That is, we construct an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm A}_{\infty}$</tex> functor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int:\mathcal R{\mathrm ep}^{\infty}(A)\rightarrow \hat {\mathcal R}{\mathrm ep}^{\infty}(\Pi_{\infty}(A))$</tex> from the representations up to homotopy of a Lie algebroid A to those of its infinity groupoid. This construction extends the usual integration of representations in Lie theory. We discuss several examples including Lie algebras and Poisson manifolds. The construction is based on an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm A}_{\infty}$</tex> version of de Rham’s theorem due to Gugenheim [15]. The integration procedure we explain here amounts to extending the construction of parallel transport for superconnections, introduced by Igusa [17] and Block–Smith [6], to the case of certain differential graded manifolds.

articleTitle: On a Question of Keating and Rudnick about Primitive Dirichlet Characters with Squarefree Conductor
abstract: We prove equidistribution results, in the function field setting, for the L-functions attached to primitive, odd Dirichlet characters with a fixed squarefree conductor.

articleTitle: A Reciprocity Formula for a Cotangent Sum
abstract: We introduce the cotangent sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c(h/k)=-\Sigma^{k-1}_{a=1}\ \frac {a}{k}\ \cot\ \frac {\pi\ ah}{k}$</tex> and prove that it satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$hc(h/k)+c(k/h)-\frac {1}{\pi k}=g(h/k)$</tex>, where g is a function which is analytic on the complex plane minus the negative real axis. The sum arises in connection with the Nyman–Beurling approach to the Riemann hypothesis.

articleTitle: Groupes Quantiques d’Interpolation de Langlands de Rang 1
abstract: On étudie une certaine famille, paramétrée par un entier <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr g \epsilon \mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}$</tex>, de doubles déformations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{h,h^'} (\mathfrak{sl_2}, \scr {g})$</tex> de l’algèbre enveloppante <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_h(\mathfrak{sl_2})$</tex>, dans l’esprit de [7]. On prouve que <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{h,h'} (\mathfrak{sl_2}, \scr {g})$</tex> déforme simultanément les groupes quantiques <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_h(\mathfrak{sl_2})$</tex> et <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{h^{'}}(\mathfrak{sl_2})$</tex>. On montre que cette propriété d’interpolation explique la dualité de Langlands pour les représentations des groupes quantiques en rang 1. On résout ainsi une conjecture de [7] dans ce cas: on prouve pour tout <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\scr g \epsilon \mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}$</tex> l’existence de représentations de <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{h,h'} (\mathfrak{sl_2}, \scr {g})$</tex> qui déforment simultanément deux représentations Langlands duales. On étudie aussi plus généralement la théorie des représentations de rang fini de <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U_{h,h'} (\mathfrak{sl_2}, \scr {g})$</tex>.

articleTitle: Rank 1 Bridgeland Stable Moduli Spaces on A Principally Polarized Abelian Surface
abstract: We compute moduli spaces of Bridgeland stable objects on an irreducible principally polarized complex abelian surface <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbb T,\ell)$</tex> corresponding to twisted ideal sheaves. We use Fourier–Mukai techniques to extend the ideas of Arcara and Bertram to express wall crossings as Mukai flops and show that the moduli spaces are projective.

articleTitle: A Priori Estimates for Fully Nonlinear Parabolic Equations
abstract: In this paper, we prove the Hölder continuity of the second derivatives <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D^2_xu$</tex> for fully nonlinear, uniformly parabolic equations. We assume the inhomogeneous term f is Hölder continuous with respect to the spatial variables x and bounded and measurable with respect to the time t. As an application, we obtain higher regularity for curvature flows with volume constraints.

articleTitle: Blow-ups of Locally Conformally Kähler Manifolds
abstract: A locally conformally Khler (LCK) manifold is a complex manifold which admits a covering endowed with a Kähler metric with respect to which the covering group acts through homotheties. We show that the blow-up of a compact LCK manifold along a complex submanifold admits an LCK structure if and only if this submanifold is globally conformally Kähler. We also prove that a twistor space (of a compact four-manifold, a quaternion-Kähler manifold, or a Riemannian manifold) cannot admit an LCK metric, unless it is Kähler.

articleTitle: Seshadri Constants of K3 Surfaces of Degrees 6 and 8
abstract: We compute Seshadri constants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon(X):=\varepsilon(\mathcal O_X(1))$</tex> on K3 surfaces X of degrees 6 and 8. We also prove that if X is any embedded K3 surface of degree 2r−2≥8 in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^r$</tex> not containing lines, then 1<ε(X)<2 if and only if the homogeneous ideal of X is not generated by only quadrics (in which case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon(X)=\frac {3}{2}$</tex>).

articleTitle: On the Quantum Homology of Real Lagrangians in Fano Toric Manifolds
abstract: Let R be the real Lagrangian in a toric symplectic manifold X, the fixed point set under complex conjugation. Assuming that X is Fano of minimal Chern number at least 2, we show that the Lagrangian quantum homology QH(R;Λ) of R over the ring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda =\mathbb{Z}_{2}[t,t^{-1}]$</tex> is isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H(R;\mathbb{Z}_{2})\otimes \Lambda$</tex> as a module. Moreover, we prove that QH(R;Λ) is isomorphic as a ring to the quantum homology QH(X;Λ) of the ambient symplectic manifold.

articleTitle: Period Functions for Maass Cusp Forms for Γ0(p): A Transfer Operator Approach
abstract: We characterize Maass cusp forms for Hecke congruence subgroups of prime level as 1-eigenfunctions of a finite-term transfer operator.

articleTitle: Monochromatic Reconstruction Algorithms for Two-dimensional Multi-channel Inverse Problems
abstract: We consider two inverse problems for the multi-channel two-dimensional Schrödinger equation at fixed positive energy, i.e., the equation −Δψ+V (x)ψ=Eψ at fixed positive E, where V is a matrix-valued potential. The first is the Gel’fand inverse problem on a bounded domain D at fixed energy and the second is the inverse fixed-energy scattering problem on the whole plane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R^{2}}$</tex>. We present in this paper two algorithms which give efficient approximate solutions to these problems: in particular, in both cases, we show that the potential V is reconstructed with Lipschitz stability by these algorithms up to O(E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−(m−2)/2</sup>) in the uniform norm as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E \rightarrow + \infty$</tex>, under the assumptions that V is m-times differentiable in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, for m≥3, and has sufficient boundary decay.

articleTitle: Hecke Eigensystems for (mod p) Modular Forms of PEL Type and Algebraic Modular Forms
abstract: We show that, under suitable assumptions, the Hecke eigensystems arising from (mod p) modular forms of PEL type associated to an algebraic group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G/\mathbb Q$</tex> of type A or C, coincide with the Hecke eigensystems arising from (mod p) algebraic modular forms associated to an inner form I of G. The form I has to be compact modulo center at infinity and satisfies: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\mathbb Q_v}=G_{\mathbb Q_v}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v\ne p,\ \infty$</tex>. In order to realize the Hecke correspondence, we first adapt a result of Rapoport and Zink to obtain an explicit uniformization of the superspecial locus of PEL Shimura varieties over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {\mathbb F}_p$</tex> (such a uniformization in the general context of PEL Shimura varieties was first described by C.-F. Yu). We then compare (mod p) modular forms with superspecial modular forms by exploiting the Hermitian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb F_{p^2}$</tex>-structure of the cotangent spaces of the p-divisible groups of the superspecial points. We study in detail the case in which G is of type A, and we prove that the number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal N$</tex> of (mod p) Hecke eigensystems arising from unitary modular forms for a fixed quadratic imaginary field, having signature (r,s), prime-to-p level N≥3 and variable weight satisfies the estimate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal N\in O(p^{g^2+g+1-rs})$</tex> for p large, where g=r+s. The paper generalizes results of J-P. Serre for GL(2) and Ghitza for GSp(2g) (g>1).

articleTitle: Monodromy at Infinity of Polynomial Maps and Newton Polyhedra (with an Appendix by C. Sabbah)
abstract: By introducing motivic Milnor fibers at infinity of polynomial maps, we propose some methods for the study of nilpotent parts of monodromies at infinity. The numbers of Jordan blocks in the monodromy at infinity will be described by the Newton polyhedron at infinity of the polynomial.

articleTitle: Layer Potential Analysis for Pseudodifferential Matrix Operators in Lipschitz Domains on Compact Riemannian Manifolds: Applications to Pseudodifferential Brinkman Operators
abstract: The goal of this paper was to develop a potential analysis for a certain type of pseudodifferential matrix operators on Lipschitz domains in compact Riemannian manifolds and apply this analysis to treat boundary value problems for general Brinkman operators on such Lipschitz domains and boundary data in various Sobolev spaces.

articleTitle: Dimensions of Group Schemes of Automorphisms of Truncated Barsotti–Tate Groups
abstract: Let D be a p-divisible group over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_D\in\mathbb N$</tex> be the smallest nonnegative integer such that D is determined by D[p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>] within the class of p-divisible groups over k of the same codimension c and dimension d as D. We study n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>, lifts of D[p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>] to truncated Barsotti–Tate groups of level m+1 over k, and the numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma_D(i):=\dim({\rm Aut}(D[p^i]))$</tex>. We show that n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>≤cd, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\gamma_D(i+1)-\gamma_D(i))_{i\in\mathbb N}$</tex> is a decreasing sequence in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb N$</tex>, for cd>0 we have γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>(1)<γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>(2)<⋯<γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>(n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>), and for m∈{1,…,n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>−1} there exists an infinite set of truncated Barsotti–Tate groups of level m+1 which are pairwise nonisomorphic and lift D[p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>]. Different generalizations to p-divisible groups with a smooth integral group scheme in the crystalline context are also proved.

articleTitle: Restrictions of Steiner Bundles and Divisors on the Hilbert Scheme of Points in the Plane
abstract: The Hilbert scheme of n points in the projective plane parameterizes degree n zero-dimensional subschemes of the projective plane. We examine the dual cones of effective divisors and moving curves on the Hilbert scheme. By studying interpolation, restriction, and stability properties of certain vector bundles on the plane, we fully determine these cones for just over three-fourths of all values of n. A general Steiner bundle on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^N$</tex> is a vector bundle E admitting a resolution of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$0\rightarrow \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^N}(-1)^s\overset{M}{\rightarrow}\mathcal O^{s+r}_{\mathbb P^N}\rightarrow E\rightarrow0,$$</tex> where the map M is general. We complete the classification of slopes of semistable Steiner bundles on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^N$</tex> by showing every admissible slope is realized by a bundle which restricts itself to a balanced bundle on a rational curve. The proof involves a basic question about multiplication of polynomials on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb P^1$</tex> which is interesting in its own right.

articleTitle: Grothendieck Classes and Chern Classes of Hyperplane Arrangements
abstract: We show that the characteristic polynomial of a hyperplane arrangement can be recovered from the class in the Grothendieck group of varieties of the complement of the arrangement. This gives a quick proof of a theorem of Orlik and Solomon relating the characteristic polynomial with the ranks of the cohomology of the complement of the arrangement. We also show that the characteristic polynomial can be computed from the total Chern class of the complement of the arrangement. In the case of free arrangements, we prove that this Chern class agrees with the Chern class of the dual of a bundle of differential forms with logarithmic poles along the hyperplanes in the arrangement; this follows from the work of Mustaţa and Schenck. We conjecture that this relation holds for any locally quasi-homogeneous free divisor. We give an explicit relation between the characteristic polynomial of an arrangement and the Segre class of its singularity (“Jacobian”) subscheme. This gives a variant of a recent result of Wakefield and Yoshinaga, and shows that the Segre class of the singularity subscheme of an arrangement together with the degree of the arrangement determines the ranks of the cohomology of its complement. We also discuss the positivity of the Chern classes of hyperplane arrangements: we give a combinatorial interpretation of this phenomenon, and discuss the cases of generic and free arrangements.

articleTitle: Jones Polynomials of Torus Knots via DAHA
abstract: We suggest a construction for the Quantum Groups–Jones polynomials of torus knots in terms of the PBW theorem of double affine Hecke algebra (DAHA) for any root systems and weights (justified for type A). The main focus is on the DAHA super-polynomials, a stable type A variant of this construction. A connection is expected with the approach to super-polynomials due to Aganagic and Shakirov via the Macdonald polynomials at roots of unity and the Verlinde algebra. The duality conjecture for the DAHA super-polynomials is stated, essentially matching that due to Gukov and Stosic. A link to Khovanov–Rozansky polynomials is provided. The hyper-polynomials of types B and C are defined, generalizing the Kauffman polynomials. The special values and other features of the DAHA super- and hyper-polynomials are discussed.
